chatMessages.text: Riya, the sales boy says families are moving in and OC will come any day. Thirty-four years in banking taught me 'any day' means no.
You are right, Suresh sir. Rule #42: No photocopied OC number, no offer. Strict is how you sleep.

monthlyLearnings.headline: "Ready-to-move" and "OC received" are not the same sentence
monthlyLearnings.body: Suresh learned to demand the occupancy certificate's number, not its existence, before opening price negotiations.

monthlyLearnings.headline: Builder-held inventory negotiates differently from launch stock
monthlyLearnings.body: Quarter-end and financial-year-end conversations produced ₹40–60L swings on identical completed units.

monthlyLearnings.headline: RWA sinking fund health is the real structural report
monthlyLearnings.body: Auditing society AGM minutes revealed unrecorded repair levies, saving ₹6L in unbudgeted maintenance.

monthlyLearnings.headline: Stopped comparing today's price to 2019 reference points
monthlyLearnings.body: Accepted current South Bengaluru market pricing — the market does not owe anyone historical reference points.

monthlyLearnings.headline: Walking away twice established real negotiation power
monthlyLearnings.body: Exiting negotiations when sellers moved final prices taught brokers Suresh was serious; the third deal started 8% lower.

checklistItems: You have meaningful savings earning FD rates, and the guilt of "doing nothing" with them has started arriving with every renewal notice.
Capital protection matters more to you than capital growth — you would take 3% safe over 12% uncertain without blinking.
You will not sign an EMI. Ever. The conversation ends there.
You only trust what you can physically visit, and you want the asset within your daily geography.
Documents calm you down; brochures make you suspicious.
A 7-year-old building with a good RWA feels safer to you than a brand-new tower with a ribbon on it.
